title.narrative: IN Madhya Pradesh Water Sector Restructuring Project

description.narrative: The Madhya Pradesh Water Sector Restructuring Project for India aims to improve productivity of water for sustainable growth, and poverty reduction in selected focus river basins (Chambal, Sindh, Betwa, Ken and Tons) of Madhya Pradesh. The project has the following four components: Component 1) will support the establishment and operationalization of the proposed planning, allocation and regulatory institutions and instruments at the state and basin-levels. Component 2) will support measures related to delivering reliable irrigation services at rationalized cost by financially viable entities. Component 3) will operationalize the concepts and provide the necessary investments in five basins (Chambal, Sindh, Betwa, Ken, and Tons) for (i) reliable delivery of water measured and supplied on an appropriate volumetric basis in the irrigation systems of these basins to improve system performance, cost recovery and accountability of the service provider; (ii) an outcome-oriented approach with integrated sustainable agricultural intensification and diversification; and (iii) improved operation and management of the irrigation and drainage schemes. Component 4) The project activities would be coordinated by a multi-disciplinary Project Implementation Coordination Unit (PICU). Support would be provided to assist the PICU with its role in facilitating and guiding the implementation and monitoring of all project activities, ensuring synergy and coordination amongst activities and agencies implementing these activities, preparing consolidated reports and facilitating training.

The project development objective is to improve productivitv of water for sustainable growth and poverty reduction in selected focus river basins (Chambal, Sindh, Betwa, Ken and Tons) of Madhya Pradesh.

title.narrative: Operational water user associations created and/or strengthened (number)

comment.narrative: The baseline refers to strengthened WUAs. In 2005, MP already had established WUAs all over the state, but they had not receivedany support and training.
It is assumed that 75-80 percent of the project WUAs are operational as per definition under the core indicators.

WUAs have been established throughout the state, including the project schemes. Strengthening has not been completed for any ofthe WUAs as the program of support and training is ongoing and will be enhanced during the next two years. A WUA performancereview is ongoing to determine the actual status of each project WUA.

baseline.value: No arrangements in place, with fragmented management of water resources.

target.value: Single State water governance body established and functioning in accordance with stated roles and responsibilities(WRM Wing, withSWaRA and SWaDRAC incorporated).

actual.value: WRM Wing has been formed and functioning with returned WRM trainees/specialists. Draft comprehensive, modern river basin plansprepared and reviewed by WRD. WRM Wing specialists now using modern tools for river basin planning and management.

title.narrative: Introduction of modern skills and tools and business process re-engineering with PPP in GoMP I&D service delivery institutions including the establishment and effective use of modern IMS.

baseline.value: Overstaffed and inadequately skilled staff in WRD; absence of computerized IMS; Irrigation Manual needs updating; no systematicPPP; PIM Act exists and WUAs formed but need to be trained.

target.value: IMS fully operational; Modern techniques incorporated in WRD operation, PPP introduced; Project scheme WUAs fully trained.

actual.value: Skills being introduced. Irrigation management exceeds expectations. Effective EMIS in place and operational for all irrigation inthe state.
